title: QpiAI Inaugurates 8-Inch Quantum Chip Foundry in Bengaluru Targeting 10,000-Qubit QPUs - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Indian full-stack quantum-and-AI startup QpiAI opened an 8-inch superconducting QPU foundry in Bengaluru capable of up to 128 physical qubits, targeting 10,000-qubit QPUs by a 2027 Phase 3, backed by a $32M Series A co-led by Avataar Ventures and India's National Quantum Mission.

insights.claim: QpiAI inaugurated an 8-inch quantum processing unit manufacturing facility in Jakkur, Bengaluru, designated Phase 2 of its 70,000-square-foot R&D center, capable of fabricating flip-chip superconducting processors with up to 128 physical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An in-house 8-inch foundry gives QpiAI vertical control over QPU fabrication, rare among quantum startups.
insights.quote: the quantum foundry can fabricate flip-chip superconducting quantum processors with up to 128 physical qubits.

insights.claim: The facility handles the full device manufacturing lifecycle on-site including electron-beam lithography, wet/dry etching, Josephson-junction fabrication, 3D flip-chip assembly, and cryogenic packaging, operating with Class 100 and Class 1,000 cleanrooms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: End-to-end on-site capability reduces supply-chain dependence and shortens QPU iteration cycles.

insights.claim: QpiAI plans to complete Phase 3 by 2027, expanding cleanroom infrastructure to fabricate single QPUs containing up to 10,000 physical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A 10,000-qubit target is an aggressive roadmap milestone against which to track execution risk.
insights.quote: The company plans to complete Phase 3 by 2027, expanding the cleanroom infrastructure to fabricate single QPUs containing up to 10,000 physical qubits.

insights.claim: QpiAI has already fabricated four processors at the site: QVidya (8-qubit transmon), Indus (25-qubit transmon in hybrid HPC data centers), Kaveri (64-qubit transmon with proprietary low-loss flip-chip interconnects), and Yukti (9-qubit fluxonium variant for fault-tolerant surface codes).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A shipping multi-chip lineup evidences real fabrication capability behind the roadmap claims.

insights.claim: QpiAI expects to deliver its 128-qubit Ganges processor as its next production milestone.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The Ganges chip is the near-term deliverable to watch for validating foundry throughput.

insights.claim: QpiAI has invested $20M-$25M USD into the facility to date and plans an additional $10M-$15M USD for Phase 3 equipment and testing capacity expansion.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Capex figures frame the scale of investment required to reach the 10,000-qubit target.
insights.quote: QpiAI has invested $20M–$25M USD into the facility to date, with plans to allocate an additional $10M–$15M USD for Phase 3 equipment and testing capacity expansion.

insights.claim: QpiAI is backed by a $32M USD Series A co-led by Avataar Ventures and India's National Quantum Mission, and is one of eight startups selected for direct equity and grant support under NQM's domestic hardware initiative.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Government co-investment through NQM signals India's sovereign push to build domestic quantum hardware capacity.

insights.claim: The foundry serves as the hardware backbone for QpiAI's planned Quantum Supremacy Centres, hybrid data centers linking fault-tolerant QPUs with AI clusters to target commercial advantage in pharmaceutical simulation, logistics, and materials science, with a primary 10-acre India campus and four planned international sites.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The hybrid QPU-AI data center concept is QpiAI's commercialization path linking hardware to revenue applications.
